mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X1 xDrive28i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: An N20B20 engine for the BMW X1 xDrive28i typically costs £1,600-£5,800 supply-only depending on condition - used units start around £1,600, reconditioned from £2,800, and fully rebuilt from £3,800. Supply & fit adds £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X1 xDrive28i N20B20 timing chain really that bad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the N20 timing chain guide failure is a well-documented issue on pre-2015 engines. The plastic chain guides can shatter without warning, leading to catastrophic engine failure. BMW issued a service bulletin but no formal UK recall. Preventative replacement at 50,000-60,000 miles is strongly recommended.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N20B20 timing chain failure in the BMW X1 xDrive28i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N20 often gives little warning, but common signs include a rattling noise on cold start, a check engine light with timing-related fault codes, and in severe cases, engine misfire or no-start condition. Some owners report a 'whining' noise from the rear of the engine as the chain guide degrades.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X1 xDrive28i N20B20 a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N20 is a mixed bag. When maintained properly and with the timing chain addressed preventatively, it can be a reliable and enjoyable engine - 245hp from a 2.0-litre four-cylinder is impressive even today. However, the timing chain guide issue is a genuine design flaw that affects almost all pre-2015 units. HPFP failures and oil leaks are also common.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW X1 xDrive28i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2011-2015 BMW X1 xDrive28i is typically worth £4,000-£10,000. A rebuilt N20B20 engine at £3,800-£5,800 supply-only represents a significant investment. On a well-maintained, higher-value example, replacement is worthwhile. On a sub-£5,000 example, a used engine or careful evaluation of scrap value is recommended.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my BMW X1 xDrive28i has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your BMW X1 xDrive28i's VIN plate under the bonnet or in the driver's door shut - the engine code is printed as an 8-11 character code. For the xDrive28i, the engine code will be N20B20, N20B20A or N20B20O0 (2011-2015), or N52B30 (2009-2011 early production). You can also enter your registration in the tool above.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X1 xDrive28i (E84) - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The xDrive28i was the performance-oriented petrol flagship of the first-generation E84 X1 range. Launched initially with BMW's naturally aspirated 3.0-litre N52 straight-six, it was completely overhauled in early 2011 when BMW introduced its first modern turbocharged four-cylinder - the N20B20 - making the X1 xDrive28i the debut vehicle for this new engine family.

milestones.description: X1 xDrive28i launched with N52B30, 3.0L naturally aspirated straight-six, 258hp, 310Nm, six-speed automatic
N20B20 2.0L turbocharged four-cylinder introduced, replacing the N52; 245hp, 350Nm from 1,250rpm, eight-speed automatic
xDrive28i receives N20B20A variant with 245hp; timing chain guide issues begin to surface in early production
E84 LCI (facelift) brings styling updates; N20 timing chain guides redesigned with improved material
E84 production ends; F48 generation replaces it with front-wheel-drive platform and B-series engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW X1 xDrive28i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points specific to the N20B20 turbo petrol unit.

commonProblems.h2: BMW X1 xDrive28i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The N20B20 engine in the BMW X1 xDrive28i delivered impressive performance when new - 245hp from a 2.0-litre four-cylinder was class-leading in 2011. However, the N20 has well-documented reliability issues that make replacement a common consideration for owners of 2011-2015 models. Timing chain guide failure is the most critical issue, followed by high-pressure fuel pump failure and oil leaks. Every rebuilt N20B20 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded timing chain components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N20B20 Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW X1 xDrive28i's Most Critical Fault Can Destroy Your Engine
problems.rootCause: The plastic timing chain guides in early N20 engines become brittle and shatter - a design flaw BMW acknowledged but never formally recalled in the UK. The chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, making access difficult. When the guides fail, the chain can skip teeth or snap completely, bending valves and destroying the engine. Unlike the N47 diesel, the N20 often gives little audible warning before catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner, oil pump drive - engine remains in car
repairOptions.longevity: Prevents catastrophic failure. Recommended at 50,000-60,000 miles as preventative maintenance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply of rebuilt unit with upgraded chain components, fitted, tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has snapped and bent valves.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2011-2015 BMW X1 xDrive28i is valued at approximately £4,000-£10,000 depending on mileage, condition and trim. A rebuilt N20B20 engine at £3,800-£5,800 supply-only represents a significant proportion of the vehicle's value. On sub-£5,000 examples, a used engine or careful evaluation of scrap value is recommended. On well-maintained, higher-value examples with full service history, a rebuilt unit is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: On an N20-powered X1 xDrive28i over 50,000 miles, the £950-£1,500 preventative chain replacement is excellent value - far cheaper than a full engine replacement. The engine rarely gives audible warning before failure; if you own one, treat this as scheduled maintenance. Post-failure, dealer repair costs often exceed the car's value; a specialist rebuilt engine is the sensible path.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N20B20 BMW X1 xDrive28i engine prices

problems.h4: N20B20 High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - A Common Cause of Poor Running
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump can fail, causing fuel pressure issues that result in long cranking, rough idle, hesitation during acceleration, and reduced power. While not as problematic as the N54's HPFP issues, it is a known weak point on higher-mileage N20 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump, fuel rail pressure sensor if required
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; restores normal fuel delivery.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply of rebuilt unit, fitted, tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if HPFP failure has caused further engine damage.

problems.recommendation: If your xDrive28i experiences long cranking before starting or hesitation under acceleration, have the HPFP diagnosed promptly. A £500-£900 specialist replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. BMW has issued technical service bulletins on N20 fuel pump issues - ensure any replacement uses the latest part revision.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW X1 xDrive28i N20B20 HPFP replacement and engine inspection

problems.h4: N20B20 Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gaskets
problems.rootCause: The valve cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket degrade over time, causing oil leaks. On the xDrive28i, the turbocharger sits close to the engine, and oil leaks around the turbocharger are particularly common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, clean oil residue
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves external oil leaks; prevents oil dripping onto exhaust.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing gasket, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves oil leaks from filter housing; prevents oil contamination of serpentine belt.

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the N20 are common but not catastrophic if addressed early. A small oil leak around the valve cover or oil filter housing is a relatively inexpensive fix at a specialist. However, if left unchecked, oil can drip onto the exhaust or turbocharger, creating a fire risk - address oil leaks promptly.
